hypotheses.title: Daytime Institutional Accumulation vs Overnight Noise Spread
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Empirical microstructure research (Lou, Polk, and Skouras 2019) documents that informed institutional order flow executes primarily during regular market hours, driving persistent daytime price trends ((close - open) / open). In contrast, overnight price gaps ((open - ts_delay(close, 1)) / ts_delay(close, 1)) are dominated by retail liquidity noise and sentiment overreaction that rapidly mean-reverts. Subtracting the overnight gap from the daytime return isolates genuine institutional accumulation with 100% instrument coverage across TOP3000.
confounders: Unscheduled earnings announcements released after market close where overnight gaps represent true fundamental information
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if daytime-overnight return spread yields Sharpe < 1.25 in TOP3000.

candidates.expression: group_rank(ts_decay_linear((close - open) / open - (open - ts_delay(close, 1)) / ts_delay(close, 1), 10), subindustry) - 0.5
candidates.rationale: Subindustry-standardized 10-day decayed spread between daytime return and overnight gap return.

hypotheses.title: High/Low Structural Time-Decay Momentum using Extreme Offsets
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Tracking the temporal recency of 20-day price extremes reveals structural order-book momentum. ts_argmax(high, 20) measures the trading days elapsed since the 20-day high (0 if today), while ts_argmin(low, 20) measures days since the 20-day low. The difference ts_argmin(low, 20) - ts_argmax(high, 20) peaks at +19 when an equity is making fresh breakout highs with distant lows, capturing pure price momentum without any price-ratio distortion or scale sensitivity.
confounders: Range-bound consolidation regimes where new 20-day highs immediately encounter overhead resistance
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if structural extreme offsets fail to achieve Sharpe >= 1.25 or Fitness >= 1.00.

candidates.rationale: Uniform subindustry rank of the difference between elapsed days to 20-day low and elapsed days to 20-day high.

hypotheses.title: Tail-Risk Kurtosis Discount and Return Distribution Predictability
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Fat-tailed return distributions (high kurtosis) reflect heightened crash vulnerability and retail lottery-ticket speculation. Using the virgin operator ts_kurtosis over a rolling 60-day window, penalizing high kurtosis (-ts_kurtosis(returns, 60)) isolates equities with Gaussian-like stability, predictable compounding, and negligible headline tail risk, generating robust risk-adjusted returns when neutralized across subindustries.
confounders: Sudden macroeconomic volatility shocks that cause broad-market return kurtosis to spike across all sectors
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if low kurtosis discount yields Sharpe < 1.25 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized uniform ranking of negative 60-day rolling return kurtosis.
